text: The workflow platform is shared platform and the replay gate contract is fixed at status Draft on Day 1 with the following working read: namespace rwb-recovery and the task queue `rwb-platform`; SIT histories only, codec-encrypted, with no production history exported; 200 closed histories per workflow type; a 24-hour freshness limit on the newest export of a type; a 10-minute gate budget and a 60-second wall-clock bound for the 30-day timer test; a 90-day replay retention; gate 10 as the tenth pipeline check in Recovery Workbench Engineering Practices; MSG-P3-038 unchanged with its {detail} fields. The pipeline identity that runs the gate, the pinned SDK version the corpus is replayed at and the owner of the build registry stay open placeholders.
why: The contract cannot be published on Day 1 without a freshness rule, a retention, a budget, a gate number and a message, and Template and Rules §R4 gives the shared platform no service row of its own; the namespace, the task queue and the gate number are stated by Architecture v5, the Ownership Map and the legacy story, so those are adopted as the working read and the remaining values are carried from the legacy configuration unchanged.
read: Temporal namespace rwb-recovery; task queue `rwb-platform`; SIT histories only and codec-encrypted; 200 histories per workflow type; 24-hour freshness; 10-minute gate budget; 60-second wall-clock bound for the 30-day timer test; 90-day replay retention; build ID format <git-sha>-<build-number>; gate 10 in Engineering Practices; MSG-P3-038 text unchanged; the pipeline identity, the pinned SDK version and the build registry owner are open.
confirm: Platform team, the pipeline owner and SCB IT architecture, at the Wave 0 Service Catalog review
impact: If the read is wrong, the index row, the gate report and the registry answers change in a v2 contract release; no business value, schema or business rule changes.
